### Stay With Us
Author: Alistair Begg
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/truth-for-life/truth-for-life-july-4-2023.html
Passage: Luke 24:28-29
Points:
- Jesus acted as if He would journey further when the disciples reached Emmaus.
- The two travelers urgently pleaded with Him to stay the night with them.
- Had they failed to invite Him in, they would have missed discovering His identity.
- Believers often attempt to handle life's anxieties alone instead of inviting Jesus in.
- Asking Christ into our difficulties grants a renewed, heart-stirring sense of His presence.

### Jesus Comes Looking for You
Author: Adrian Rogers
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/loveworthfinding/love-worth-finding-april-18-2026.html
Passage: Luke 24:15
Points:
- Jesus took the initiative to draw near and accompany the two travelers.
- He came alongside them not to condemn their confusion, but to comfort them.
- Just as Christ seeks the lost, He faithfully pursues believers who wander or despair.
- Experiencing the Lord's persistent pursuit reassures believers of His grace.
- Christ's seeking love should motivate believers to reach out with the gospel to others.

### Look beyond discouragement
Author: Jack Graham
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/powerpoint/powerpoint-mar-31-2010-11628252.html
Passage: Luke 24:21
Points:
- The Emmaus travelers were overwhelmed by the shattering of their messianic expectations.
- Intense discouragement kept them from realizing the risen Lord was walking with them.
- Many believers today live as though Christ never conquered the grave.
- Fixating on sorrow and dashed dreams blinds people to God's active presence.
- Remembering that Jesus lives restores courage, hope, and strength.

### The Master Teacher
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/the-master-teacher
Passage: Luke 24:32
Points:
- Jesus gently rebuked the travelers' despondency by opening the Old Testament to them.
- He showed that the prophetic Scriptures required the Messiah to suffer before entering glory.
- Recognizing Jesus in the breaking of bread brought clarity to their earlier conversation.
- Hearing God's Word centered on Christ ignites warmth within cold, sluggish hearts.
- Christians are called to examine whether their hearts remain warm and receptive to God.
